book_short: Kieso, Weygandt, Warfield and Wiley, Intermediate Accounting (19th edition)
book_meta: Donald E. Kieso, Jerry J. Weygandt, Terry D. Warfield and Laura D. Wiley. Wiley, 2025. WileyPLUS optional.

intro: A continuation of ACCT 416 Intermediate Accounting I (ACCT 311 at some institutions). Topics: intangible assets, current liabilities, long-term liabilities, stockholders' equity, earnings per share, revenue recognition, investments, accounting changes and the statement of cash flows. Prerequisite: C- or better in ECON 201, ECON 202 and ACCT 311 or ACCT 416. The running case continues with Bluestem Outdoor of Marshall, Minnesota as it buys a competitor, issues bonds, goes public, rewards employees with stock and builds a long-term contract business, with CFO Maria Okafor and controller Sam Nygaard.
book_note: The standard US intermediate accounting text, closely aligned with the CPA exam. ACCT 312 and ACCT 416 share this one book and split its chapters between them with no overlap: if you took ACCT 416, you already own it.
book_split: ACCT 312 reads Chapters 12–18, 22 and 23. ACCT 416 Intermediate Accounting I reads Chapters 1–11. Chapters 19–21 and 24 (income taxes, pensions, leases, full disclosure) aren't part of either course.
reading_note: The whole semester's reading in one table. Chapters follow the textbook's order, with Chapters 14 to 18 each spread over two lectures.
